title: A Controlled Comparison of Deep Learning Architectures for Multi-Horizon Financial Forecasting Evidence from 918 Experiments
content: Reliable comparison of deep learning architectures for financial forecasting requires controlled evaluation that separates architectural effects from hyperparameter tuning, random initialization, forecast horizon, and asset characteristics. We present a five-stage benchmark designed to provide a systematic and reproducible comparison through equal-budget Bayesian hyperparameter optimization, category-level configuration freezing, three-seed final training, held-out metric aggregation, and rank-based statistical validation. Nine architectures spanning Transformer, MLP/linear, convolutional, and recurrent families are evaluated using direct multi-step prediction from five OHLCV features across 12 assets (four cryptocurrency, four foreign exchange, and four equity-index instruments), with chronological 70/15/15 splits of 30,000 hourly windows per asset at 4- and 24-hour forecasting horizons. The benchmark comprises 918 runs, including 270 optimization trials and 648 final training runs. Across 24 asset--horizon evaluation points, ModernTCN achieves a mean rank of 1.333 and the lowest root mean squared error (RMSE) in 18 points (75.0%), followed by PatchTST with a mean rank of 2.000. The global ranking differences are strongly supported by an Iman--Davenport test (\( F(8,184)=101.36 \), \( p<10^{-15} \)), with 33 of 36 Holm-adjusted pairwise comparisons statistically significant. Architectural rankings also exhibit strong cross-horizon consistency across all 12 assets (\( \rho\geq0.683 \); Stouffer \( p=3.47\times10^{-10} \)), while forecasting errors increase at the longer horizon. Architecture accounts for 99.90% of raw error variance and 68.33% after within-slot normalization excluding LSTM, whereas seed variance contributes at most 0.04% (0.02% without LSTM). Mean directional accuracy reaches 50.08%. Overall, the findings establish a statistically validated comparison of nine forecasting architectures and identify ModernTCN and PatchTST as leading performers under the evaluated experimental conditions, providing a reproducible benchmark for systematic architecture selection in multi-asset financial time-series forecasting.
